content.content:
# Message List

## Concept

### Pitch

The chat history of prompt mode: the prompts sent to the harness and its responses, as a conversation.

### Shape

#### Description

Conversation-style, shows send prompts on the right, received input on the left.

#### Sent Prompt

A sent prompt shows the compiled markdown that was actually sent to the harness, rendered as markdown, once it has compiled. Its message header shows the name of the hidden anchor it was compiled from.

#### Response

A response from the harness is grouped by general type, in the order it happened. The harness's own text is shown as markdown. Tool calls in a row that share a general type (reading and searching files, editing files, running commands, the web, agents, and anything else) are gathered into one group, headed by that type and how many calls it holds. Each call in a group lists the tool's name, its most telling argument, and whether it is running, done, or failed, spelled out rather than only coloured.

#### Running Skeleton

A skeleton stands in for a currently running task only while there is nothing meaningful to show for it. As soon as there is anything meaningful to display for that task in the message list, no skeleton is shown for it at all.

#### Queue Background

The header along the top of the message list, holding the pinned prompt and the queue, has the same background colour as the tab bar.

#### Legibility

The output from a realtime agent should be readable and meaningful.  Make sure the font size is large enough, that the colours are legible.

p='src/prompt_mode.rs'; s=open(p).read()
old="""                    summary => h_flex()"""
new="""                    // A known tool whose input is on its way shows only a
                    // skeleton, with nothing else beside it.
                    None if row.is_partial()
                        && ToolKind::of(&call.name).pending_input().is_some() =>
                    {
                        Skeleton::new().w(relative(0.6)).h_4().rounded_md().into_any_element()
                    }
                    summary => h_flex()"""
assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new)
old="""                        // Its input is on its way.
                        .when(row.is_partial(), |row| {
                            row.child(
                                div()
                                    .flex_1()
                                    .min_w_0()
                                    .child(tool_input_pending(call, reply, cx)),
                            )
                        })"""
new="""                        // Its input is on its way, and there is no telling
                        // what it will be.
                        .when(row.is_partial(), |row| {
                            row.child(div().flex_1().min_w_0().child(raw_tail(reply, cx)))
                        })"""
assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new)
a=s.index("/// What a running tool call shows while its input streams in")
b=s.index("/// The harness's latest raw output, standing in")
s=s[:a]+s[b:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

content.text:
Now, while a known tool's input is still coming in (Bash, Read, Edit, web or agent calls), its Output cell in the task table shows only the skeleton. The tool name ("Bash") and the "Writing the command…" line are gone. It builds without errors and the 19 prompt mode tests pass. I haven't run the app to look at it.

- **What's still there:** the "Command" badge in the Type column and the status column stay. They're separate columns, so I read your request as being about the Output cell only.
- **Other tools:** tools with no known type (e.g. MCP tools) have no skeleton. They still show their name next to the harness's latest raw output while their input comes in.
- **Collapsed row:** the one-line row outside the table has no skeleton. It still shows "Writing the command…", and I didn't change it.

The change is in `src/prompt_mode.rs`: a new case in `output_table` draws just the skeleton, and I deleted the old helper, `tool_input_pending`, which drew the label and skeleton together.
